reference_drawer.description: Fundamental trigonometric identities and proof tools.

items.rule: Sine, cosine and tangent are side ratios relative to a chosen acute angle.
items.example: In a 3-4-5 triangle, choose the reference angle before assigning sides.

items.rule: The hypotenuse square equals the sum of the squares of the legs.
items.example: Use the positive square root for a side length.

items.rule: Cosecant, secant and cotangent are reciprocals.
The acute angles of a right triangle are complementary.
From a·cotθ=b, isolate cotθ before rewriting the requested expression.
items.example: Then tanθ is the reciprocal of cotθ.

concepts.title: 1. Trigonometric Ratios
concepts.subtitle: Opposite, adjacent and hypotenuse
concepts.summary: For an acute angle in a right triangle, sine is opposite/hypotenuse, cosine is adjacent/hypotenuse and tangent is opposite/adjacent. Reciprocal functions give cosecant, secant and cotangent.

points.text: Map the three sides relative to that angle.

concepts.trap: Confusing opposite and adjacent when the reference angle changes.

concepts.title: 2. Pythagorean Connection
concepts.subtitle: Find the missing side
concepts.summary: The sides of a right triangle satisfy a²+b²=c², where c is the hypotenuse.
concepts.trap: Using the hypotenuse as a leg or taking a negative length.

concepts.title: 3. Composite Trigonometric Expressions
concepts.subtitle: Substitute and simplify
concepts.summary: Evaluate each basic trigonometric component first, then perform the indicated algebraic operation.
concepts.trap: Replacing a function by its reciprocal.

concepts.title: 4. Cotangent as a Parameter
concepts.subtitle: Use a·cotθ=b
concepts.summary: Isolate cotθ from a·cotθ=b, then rewrite sin/cos quotients using tan or cot.
concepts.trap: Forgetting to isolate cotangent before substitution.

concepts.title: 5. Finding Side Lengths
concepts.subtitle: Use a ratio plus one known side
concepts.summary: Treat the given trig ratio as a prototype side relationship, find the scale factor from the known side, then scale the remaining sides.
concepts.trap: Treating ratio numbers as actual side lengths without scaling.
